source.title: Hard-Wiring the Induction Head: The Surprising Effectiveness of Copy Mechanisms in Data-Efficient Language Modelling

page_placements.theme: Training data effects on copying ability

record.tranche_reason: The study uses targeted interventions and synthetic copying tests to evaluate a fixed induction operator's copying and layer-composition behaviour, rather than measuring emergent induction heads in the original transformer setup.
record.gate_note: The study measures copying, link use, and two-step retrieval for its operator. It does not measure induction-head formation during ordinary transformer training, token-index loss changes, or a loss-curve bump. The natural-text repetition rates, validation perplexity, benchmark scores, and efficiency results do not directly measure the claimed induction-head behaviour and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds a fixed, non-learned look-back-and-copy operator into an attention-free model and measures how its own operator is used. It induces the behaviour on purpose and does not study induction heads emerging in transformers. So it tests no version. The only measurement of copying arising on its own is the attention baseline's probe accuracy (R2). That is one training run with no analysis of heads, mechanism or data variation, so it fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that building in an exact look-back-and-copy operator makes a small attention-free model markedly more data-efficient. It stays within about 7% of a parameter-matched attention model's perplexity at convergence (34.3 vs 31.9), and its BLiMP score falls between the two GPT-2 baselines. They also conclude the operator is used, necessary and composes into two-step retrieval, and is cheaper than Flash attention beyond ~1,000 tokens. They suggest it may complement attention.
record.recipe_differences: The study hard-wires a non-learned look-back-and-copy operator in an attention-free architecture; it does not reproduce emergent attention-head formation or previous-token-head composition.
record.method_sensitivity: The source-corruption effect grows from early to late layers; two-step retrieval succeeds with two layers but not one; left-context recoverability is 76% with convolution on and 16% with it off.

fits_no_version.finding: A parameter-matched 12.3M three-layer self-attention (plus convolution) model trained on BabyLM Strict-Small reaches only about 0.05 accuracy on a repeated-half copying probe after ~100M words. It starts from almost zero. The hard-wired operator model scores about 0.5 from the start.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small attention models trained on child-scale data (~10M words, ~100M tokens seen) barely acquire induction-style repeated-sequence copying within that budget.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Second BabyLM Workshop
record.problems: The copying probe and two-step retrieval task are constructed tests; the two-step result is synthetic. The paper notes that the unused-link control was available only for a small subset of predictions. Several intervention values are shown only in figures, and the study does not test emergent induction heads in standard transformers.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results left out. Natural-text repetition percentages, validation perplexity, benchmark metrics, and runtime/memory results were excluded because they do not directly measure induction-head copying or its formation.

untested.parts: No learned induction head, previous-token head or composition in an attention-only transformer is examined; the operator is hard-coded.
No tracking of when induction heads form, of in-context learning or of the loss bump.
No measurement of in-context learning by token index, and no large models.
No search for induction heads across models.
No variation of data or training to see whether heads form.

record.verdict_notes: The study is an architecture paper that uses the induction-head idea as a design tool. All interventions (R3–R17) validate the study's own fixed operator. The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1 labels are withdrawn. The background statements on abrupt emergence and the two-layer requirement are citations of Olsson et al., not results. The sole observational result on emergent copying (R2) is a single attention baseline with three seeds and no head-level analysis.

versions.untested_parts: The operator is supplied directly rather than learned to emerge. The study does not test composition with an earlier previous-token attention head in an attention-only transformer.

relation.reason: The induction mechanism motivates a fixed architectural operator. Interventions test this supplied operator, rather than the claim versions concerning learned induction heads.

tranche.reason: The study builds copying into its architecture and evaluates its performance and use. It does not identify emergent induction heads or test any listed claim version; the attention comparator measures copying accuracy without identifying heads.

source_check.notes: Row states describe copying performance only; neither row establishes induction-head formation. Section 5.1 reports 100M words, whereas Section 4 describes total exposure as about 98 million tokens; the source contains this discrepancy.
